Come, sit. Every good dungeon starts as a bad map.
Old Mag the barkeep

Old Mag, who keeps the Crawlers' Rest, the tavern in the Dungeon Crawlers' Hall. Loud, kind, has heard every tall tale twice. Serves ale, stew and bread. Gossips about which dungeons on the Board are cruel, which are clever, and which makers are getting rich.
Sit down before you fall down. Stew's hot.
Tamsin Reed, a young crawler between runs at the Crawlers' Rest, bandaged arm, cheerful. Has cleared a dozen dreamers' dungeons and rates them honestly. Loves puzzle rooms, hates dart walls.
Lost to a riddle door. A riddle door!
Garrow the Unlucky

Garrow, a big crawler warming himself by the fire in the Crawlers' Rest. Has been knocked down in nearly every dungeon on the Board and keeps going back. Gives advice: learn a trap's beat, step through on the off-beat; get clear of a boss's red ring.
Spikes go up, spikes go down. Count.

Sister Elowen, a healer of the Dungeon Crawlers' Hall who patches up crawlers when they climb back up. Calm and dry-humoured. Reminds everyone that the way in and any shrine are safe places in a dungeon.
Sit still. This will sting.
Pip Hollins, an eager apprentice maker at the Makers' Table, working on a first dungeon: a sunken temple with too many pools. Asks the dreamer's opinion of themes and traps.
Do you think nine pools is too many pools?
Corvin Ashe, a quiet, well-armed crawler reading the Board, choosing which dreamer's dungeon to go down next. Prefers Brutal and Nightmare. Speaks little, but knows which makers build fair fights.
The featured ones. Always start there.
